Public test post, a longer one that needs several chunks. Our neighborhood garden club met on Saturday morning to plan the spring planting. We agreed to grow tomatoes, beans, squash and sunflowers in the raised beds along the south fence, and to keep the herb spiral near the gate where the light is best. Volunteers will water on a rota, two people each evening, and the tool shed key stays with the treasurer. Children from the primary school will visit in May to sow seeds and learn how compost works. Everyone is welcome to join; bring gloves, a hat and a bottle of water.
